title: Hebrew II: Intermediate Biblical Hebrew and Exegesis
description: Builds on Hebrew I with the derived verb stems (Niphal, Piel, Pual, Hiphil, Hophal, Hithpael), weak verbs, Hebrew syntax, poetry and textual criticism, and moves into exegesis of narrative, law, poetry and prophecy. Drills draw real verbs of each stem from the Hebrew Bible and check answers against STEPBible's morphology tags. The course ends with an exegetical paper based on the student's own translation of a Hebrew passage.

What is the Ketiv/Qere system?
quiz_bank.answer_key: Where the Masoretes preserved the written consonants (Ketiv) but believed another reading should be pronounced (Qere), they marked the Qere with vowels and a marginal note; STEPBible's TAHOT tags such readings.

quiz_bank.question: How do scholars decide between textual variants?
quiz_bank.answer_key: They weigh external evidence (age, quality and spread of witnesses such as MT, DSS, LXX) and internal evidence (which reading best explains the others, scribal tendencies, context, author's style), preferring the reading that best explains the rise of the others.
